name: Falls Park
unique: The falls that gave the city its name, where the Big Sioux drops over pink quartzite ledges in a downtown park with a viewing tower and the remains of a mill.
buzz: The falls and the tower are the photograph and the park is free; the lights at night in summer are the local tradition.

name: Washington Pavilion
unique: A 1890s school building turned arts and science center, with a visual arts museum, a discovery center and a domed theater.
buzz: The science center is the family draw and the art galleries are quiet; the building itself is the landmark on the downtown skyline.

name: Sioux Falls SculptureWalk
unique: A rotating outdoor gallery of 60 sculptures along the downtown streets, each for sale, with a map that turns the city into a gallery.
buzz: The walk is free and the pieces change every year; locals vote on a favorite and the winner is bought for the city.

name: Dacotah Prairie Museum
unique: A county museum in a 1911 bank building with a prairie town street, a one room school and the story of the Dakota conflict.
buzz: The street scene and the school are good with children and the collection is local and specific; it is free will donation.

name: Storybook Land
unique: A free storybook park with nursery rhyme buildings, a small train and a yellow brick road, in a town that takes its L. Frank Baum connection seriously.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for children under eight and the train is the hit; the rides cost a few dollars.

name: Lewis and Clark Lake
unique: A reservoir on the Missouri below Gavins Point Dam with 90 miles of shoreline, sandy beaches and some of the best walleye fishing in the state.
buzz: The lake is the summer water for the region and the dam is the history; the wind makes afternoon boating rough.

name: South Dakota Cultural Heritage Center
unique: The state history museum with a strong Native American collection, a sod house and the story of the Black Hills gold rush, on the capitol grounds.
buzz: The Native galleries and the sod house are the reasons to stop; it is a good rainy day and the capital building next door is free.

name: South Dakota State Capitol
unique: A Neoclassical capitol with a copper dome and a rotunda of native stone, in a town of 14,000 on the Missouri.
buzz: The rotunda and the governor's reception room are the quick tour and it is free; the view from the capitol steps is the prairie.

name: Redlin Art Center
unique: A gallery built to hold 160 Terry Redlin paintings of small town and wildlife America, given free to the public by the artist.
buzz: The scale of the gift and the building are the surprise; it is free and the paintings are more nostalgic than kitsch.

name: South Dakota Art Museum
unique: A university museum with the Harvey Dunn prairie paintings and a Marghab linen collection, free on the South Dakota State campus.
buzz: The Dunn paintings are the reason art people stop and the linens are the surprise; it is free and takes an hour.

name: McCrory Gardens
unique: Twenty five acres of display gardens and a prairie restoration on the university campus, with a children's garden and a rose garden.
buzz: The prairie and the trial gardens are the reason gardeners come and it is free; peak bloom is July.

name: The Mammoth Site
unique: A sinkhole where 60 mammoths fell in and died 26,000 years ago, now an active dig inside a building over the bone bed.
buzz: The bone bed is the real thing and the paleontologists work in front of you in summer; children can join a dig with a reservation.

name: Evans Plunge
unique: A naturally warm mineral spring pool with a water slide, the oldest attraction in the Black Hills, in a sandstone building over the spring.
buzz: The water is 87 degrees and the slide is a surprise in a historic bathhouse; it is a good family stop after the Mammoth Site.

name: Spearfish Canyon
unique: A 22 mile limestone canyon with three waterfalls, a scenic byway and trails to Bridal Veil Falls, 15 minutes from Spearfish.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the falls are short walks; it is the setting for Dances with Wolves and the canyon is busy in fall.

name: Adams Museum
unique: A museum in a 1892 brick building with Wild Bill Hickok's guns, a two headed calf and the nugget that started the gold rush.
buzz: The collection is odd and local and the building is the setting; it is cheap and pairs with the town walk.

name: Bear Butte State Park
company: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks
unique: A sacred butte where Lakota and Cheyenne people still come for vision quests, with a trail to the summit and prayer offerings along the way.
buzz: The climb is steep and the site is sacred, so visitors are asked to stay on the trail and respect the offerings; the view reaches the Black Hills.

name: Needles Highway
unique: A 14 mile road through granite spires and two tunnels blasted through the rock, including a one lane eye of the needle passage.
buzz: The tunnels and the Cathedral Spires are the photographs and the road is narrow; drive it early to avoid the tour buses.

name: Reptile Gardens
unique: A 1937 reptile park with the largest collection in the world, alligator and snake shows, and a prairie dog town you can walk through.
buzz: Children love the shows and adults are surprised by the botanical gardens; the park is old fashioned and well run.

name: Allerton Park
unique: A 1,500 acre estate with a formal garden, a brick-walled mansion and sculptures in the woods including the Fu Dog Garden.
buzz: The Fu Dog Garden and the sunken garden are the surprises and it is free; the park is between Champaign and Decatur and easy to miss.

name: Krannert Art Museum
unique: A university museum with a strong collection of European painting, African art and contemporary work, free to the public.
buzz: The permanent collection is better than expected and the shows rotate often; it is free and the café is a campus meeting spot.

name: Japan House
unique: A Japanese house and tea garden on the university campus, used for tea ceremonies and open to walk through.
buzz: The garden is the quiet corner of campus and the tea ceremonies need booking; it is free and small.

name: Peoria Riverfront Museum
unique: A combined art, history and science museum on the Illinois River with a giant screen theater and a dome planetarium.
buzz: The riverfront view and the planetarium are the reasons to go and the galleries are small; the museum is good with children on a rainy day.

name: Caterpillar Visitors Center
unique: A visitor center with a 797 mining truck, a simulator and the story of the tractors that changed farming, in the company's hometown.
buzz: The big machines and the simulator are the family draw and the history of the company is the adult part; it is indoors and cheap.

name: Anderson Japanese Gardens
unique: Twelve acres of pond, stream and strolling garden designed by a Japanese master gardener, with a tea house and a waterfall.
buzz: Gardeners call it the best Japanese garden in the midwest and the koi are the family draw; the spring and fall are the peak seasons.

name: Burpee Museum of Natural History
unique: A natural history museum with Jane, a juvenile T. rex, and a working paleontology lab, on the Rock River.
buzz: Jane is the reason children ask to come and the lab is where visitors can watch preparation; the museum is small and cheap.

name: Beer Nuts Factory
unique: The factory store where the sweet and salty peanuts have been made since 1937, with a window into the roasting room and a wall of merchandise.
buzz: The smell is the attraction and the store sells warm samples; it is a quick stop and the brand is a central Illinois institution.

name: Miller Park Zoo
unique: A small zoo in a city park with a rainforest building, a carousel and river otters, old enough to have been a city fixture since 1890.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for toddlers and the rainforest building is the winter stop; it is cheap and never crowded.

name: Villa Kathrine
unique: A Moorish revival villa on the bluffs above the Mississippi, built by a wealthy traveler who never lived in it, with a courtyard and a view of the river.
buzz: The house is strange and photogenic and the river view is the reason to climb the hill; the tour is short and the restoration is ongoing.
